acceptanceCriteria.statement: On the home route, the value proposition is readable above the fold before any secondary content or action.
The navigation order remains consistent between home and pricing as a retained structural principle.
Across both inspected routes, one primary call to action is present and no competing primary conversion action is introduced.
At mobile widths, the home hero collapses into a single vertical stack and the primary action remains reachable without horizontal scrolling.
At mobile widths, pricing tiers stack vertically and preserve their tier hierarchy.
Keyboard focus remains visibly detectable on navigation and call-to-action elements on both inspected routes.
The migrated surface does not reproduce source-specific copy, wordmark, exact palette, or unique illustrations.

accessibilityAndRecovery: Any actionable element must expose a visible focus state that survives custom theming and remains distinct at all supported breakpoints.
If a narrow viewport risks overflow, content must reflow to a single column before any text is clipped or hidden.
If pricing comparison becomes difficult on mobile, the hierarchy must be reinforced through order and labeling rather than additional visual effects.
If a new visual treatment reduces contrast or obscures focus indicators, the system must revert to a higher-contrast state for those interactive elements.
If the primary call to action is moved in the layout, it must remain reachable without requiring horizontal scrolling or nonstandard interaction patterns.
assumptions: The exact typography system is not specified in the brief, so type scale and font family are assumed to be newly authored within the original visual system.
The precise labels of the navigation items are not supplied, so only their order is treated as a retained structural constraint.
The number of pricing tiers is not specified in the brief, so the design assumes the tier count visible in the inspected snapshot without inventing new tiers.
The brief does not specify the exact primary call to action text, so CTA wording is assumed to be newly written and branded independently.

principles: Keep the inspected navigation item order as a stable structural cue while rewriting all labels and brand expression.
Preserve the home-page hero hierarchy so the value proposition is the first read, then supporting detail, then the primary action.
Use a single primary call to action across inspected pages; avoid adding secondary conversion pathways that compete for attention.
Translate the pricing page into stacked tier cards at mobile sizes so tier comparison remains legible without horizontal movement.
Preserve focus visibility and keyboard reachability on every actionable element, especially the primary call to action and navigation links.
Do not reuse source-specific copy, palette, logo treatment, or illustration motifs; any visual system must be newly authored.
globalDirection.summary: Retain the inspected marketing structure as an original B2B adaptation: a top-level navigation with the same item order, a value-proposition-led hero on home, and vertically stacked pricing tiers on the pricing route. Replace source-specific brand expression with new copy, new visual treatment, and a single dominant call to action that remains reachable on mobile without horizontal scrolling.

accessibility: Keep the primary call to action in the tab order directly after the main headline and supporting text.
Preserve a visible focus indicator that is distinguishable from surrounding page styling.
Ensure the stacked mobile hero preserves reading order from headline to supporting detail to action.
failureAndRecovery: If the hero copy becomes too long to fit above the fold, reduce supporting text before reducing the headline or removing the primary action.
If any breakpoint introduces horizontal overflow, collapse the hero and CTAs into a single-column flow before content truncation.
If focus indication is obscured by a custom theme, restore an explicit outline or equivalent visible state.
mobileRules: hero columns collapse to a single vertical stack at the mobile breakpoint
primary call to action remains reachable without horizontal scroll
screenBlueprints.summary: An original home route that introduces the offer above the fold with a stacked hero structure at mobile sizes and a single primary call to action.

accessibility: Make each tier card readable without side-to-side scrolling on small screens.
Keep the primary call to action available from the pricing route without requiring a separate path or modal.
Maintain visible keyboard focus on navigation, tier actions, and any comparison controls if present.
failureAndRecovery: If tier content overflows at mobile widths, move details under the tier title and price rather than creating a horizontal carousel.
If the hierarchy between tiers becomes ambiguous, reinforce it with position, emphasis, and labeling rather than color alone.
If any action loses focus visibility, restore a persistent focus state before shipping.
mobileRules: pricing tiers stack vertically and preserve their tier hierarchy at the mobile breakpoint
screenBlueprints.summary: An original pricing route that presents tier comparisons as vertically stacked cards at mobile sizes while keeping the same navigation structure and a single primary call to action.

sourceDecisions.rationale: Preserve the inspected navigation item order as a generic structural principle so the home and pricing routes feel continuous when moving between pages.
Keep the hero-first reading order observed on the home route so the value proposition is understood immediately above the fold.
Retain the observed mobile collapse of the home hero into a single vertical stack to avoid horizontal scrolling and preserve reading order.
Retain the observed mobile stacking of pricing tiers so comparison remains legible at narrow widths.
Preserve keyboard focus handling observed in the brief so interactive elements remain trackable during navigation.
Keep one dominant action across the inspected pages to satisfy the required conversion path while avoiding competing prompts.
Replace source-specific palette, wordmark, and illustration language with newly authored visual treatment because the adaptation must be original.
Rewrite all page copy so the adaptation communicates the same jobs without reproducing proprietary wording.
Do not carry over exact logo, branded palette, or distinctive illustration motifs because the brief forbids source-specific reproduction.
Avoid adding extra conversion prompts that dilute the single required primary call to action.
Do not replace stacked pricing tiers with a sideways carousel because that would undermine narrow-screen comparison and mobile hierarchy.
